newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares volatile after cbank intervention.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares volatile after cbank intervention.

text.p: The Czech stock market was hit by nervousness and volatility during Thursday's continuous trading session after the Czech National Bank (CNB) intervened to support the crown in the morning, dealers said.
The RPIX index of 11 continuously traded issues closed down 9.3 points, or 0.87 percent, from Wednesday at 1,064.5.

"Everybody's waiting for what's going to happen next. If foreign investors evaluate the intervention news as bad, they'll go ahead with offers of large blocks and the market will go down pretty much," said Tomas Michalek of Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.

"The volatility is discouraging investors from investing," added Daniel Gladis of Atlantik FT. "A slowly-declining crown would not be a problem, but investors mind that it is declining fast," he told Reuters.
The central bank intervened in two waves after the crown fell by over a percentage point in early trading to five percent below the midpoint its mark/dollar basket.
At 1215 GMT the crown was at -3.56 percent versus the basket mid-point.
Over 48 deals were made during the continuous session, with turnover of 26.5 million crowns.
"There are offers here of larger volumes of the three big issues, but demand is weak," said Michalek.
Dealers said the performance of individual companies would be affected by the uncertain macroeconomic climate of the country.
"In this climate (of exchange and interest rate volatility) companies cannot show solid profits. Long-term investors will rather sell than buy," Michalek said.
